title: GOVERN
source_ref: NIST AI 100-1, Section 5

title: GOVERN 1
source_text: Policies, processes, procedures, and practices across the organization related to the mapping, measuring, and managing of AI risks are in place, transparent, and implemented effectively.
source_ref: NIST AI 100-1, Table 1

title: GOVERN 1.1
source_text: Legal and regulatory requirements involving AI are understood, managed, and documented.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: GOVERN 1.2
source_text: The characteristics of trustworthy AI are integrated into organizational policies, processes, procedures, and practices.
note: Playbook wording: The characteristics of trustworthy AI are integrated into organizational policies, processes, and procedures.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: GOVERN 1.3
source_text: Processes, procedures, and practices are in place to determine the needed level of risk management activities based on the organization’s risk tolerance.
note: Playbook wording: Processes and procedures are in place to determine the needed level of risk management activities based on the organization's risk tolerance.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: GOVERN 1.4
source_text: The risk management process and its outcomes are established through transparent policies, procedures, and other controls based on organizational risk priorities.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: GOVERN 1.5
source_text: Ongoing monitoring and periodic review of the risk management process and its outcomes are planned, organizational roles and responsibilities are clearly defined, including determining the frequency of periodic review.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: GOVERN 1.6
source_text: Mechanisms are in place to inventory AI systems and are resourced according to organizational risk priorities.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: GOVERN 1.7
source_text: Processes and procedures are in place for decommissioning and phasing out of AI systems safely and in a manner that does not increase risks or decrease the organization’s trustworthiness.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: GOVERN 2
source_text: Accountability structures are in place so that the appropriate teams and individuals are empowered, responsible, and trained for mapping, measuring, and managing AI risks.
source_ref: NIST AI 100-1, Table 1

title: GOVERN 2.1
source_text: Roles and responsibilities and lines of communication related to mapping, measuring, and managing AI risks are documented and are clear to individuals and teams throughout the organization.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: GOVERN 2.2
source_text: The organization’s personnel and partners receive AI risk management training to enable them to perform their duties and responsibilities consistent with related policies, procedures, and agreements.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: GOVERN 2.3
source_text: Executive leadership of the organization takes responsibility for decisions about risks associated with AI system development and deployment.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: GOVERN 3
source_text: Workforce diversity, equity, inclusion, and accessibility processes are prioritized in the mapping, measuring, and managing of AI risks throughout the lifecycle.
source_ref: NIST AI 100-1, Table 1

title: GOVERN 3.1
source_text: Decision-makings related to mapping, measuring, and managing AI risks throughout the lifecycle is informed by a diverse team (e.g., diversity of demographics, disciplines, experience, expertise, and backgrounds).
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: GOVERN 3.2
source_text: Policies and procedures are in place to define and differentiate roles and responsibilities for human-AI configurations and oversight of AI systems.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: GOVERN 4
source_text: Organizational teams are committed to a culture that considers and communicates AI risk.
source_ref: NIST AI 100-1, Table 1

title: GOVERN 4.1
source_text: Organizational policies, and practices are in place to foster a critical thinking and safety-first mindset in the design, development, deployment, and uses of AI systems to minimize negative impacts.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: GOVERN 4.2
source_text: Organizational teams document the risks and potential impacts of the AI technology they design, develop, deploy, evaluate and use, and communicate about the impacts more broadly.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: GOVERN 4.3
source_text: Organizational practices are in place to enable AI testing, identification of incidents, and information sharing.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: GOVERN 5
source_text: Processes are in place for robust engagement with relevant AI actors.
source_ref: NIST AI 100-1, Table 1

title: GOVERN 5.1
source_text: Organizational policies and practices are in place to collect, consider, prioritize, and integrate feedback from those external to the team that developed or deployed the AI system regarding the potential individual and societal impacts related to AI risks.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: GOVERN 5.2
source_text: Mechanisms are established to enable the team that developed or deployed AI systems to regularly incorporate adjudicated feedback from relevant AI actors into system design and implementation.
note: Playbook wording: Mechanisms are established to enable AI actors to regularly incorporate adjudicated feedback from relevant AI actors into system design and implementation.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: GOVERN 6
source_text: Policies and procedures are in place to address AI risks and benefits arising from third-party software and data and other supply chain issues.
source_ref: NIST AI 100-1, Table 1

title: GOVERN 6.1
source_text: Policies and procedures are in place that address AI risks associated with third-party entities, including risks of infringement of a third party’s intellectual property or other rights.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: GOVERN 6.2
source_text: Contingency processes are in place to handle failures or incidents in third-party data or AI systems deemed to be high-risk.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: MAP
source_ref: NIST AI 100-1, Section 5

title: MAP 1
source_text: Context is established and understood.
source_ref: NIST AI 100-1, Table 2

title: MAP 1.1
source_text: Intended purposes, potentially beneficial uses, context-specific laws, norms and expectations, and prospective settings in which the AI system will be deployed are understood and documented. Considerations include: the specific set or types of users along with their expectations; potential positive and negative impacts of system uses to individuals, communities, organizations, society, and the planet; assumptions and related limitations about AI system purposes, uses, and risks across the development or product AI lifecycle; and related TEVV and system metrics.
note: Playbook wording: Intended purpose, potentially beneficial uses, context-specific laws, norms and expectations, and prospective settings in which the AI system will be deployed are understood and documented. Considerations include: specific set or types of users along with their expectations; potential positive and negative impacts of system uses to individuals, communities, organizations, society, and the planet; assumptions and related limitations about AI system purposes; uses and risks across the development or product AI lifecycle; TEVV and system metrics.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: MAP 1.2
source_text: Inter-disciplinary AI actors, competencies, skills and capacities for establishing context reflect demographic diversity and broad domain and user experience expertise, and their participation is documented. Opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration are prioritized.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: MAP 1.3
source_text: The organization’s mission and relevant goals for the AI technology are understood and documented.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: MAP 1.4
source_text: The business value or context of business use has been clearly defined or – in the case of assessing existing AI systems – re-evaluated.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: MAP 1.5
source_text: Organizational risk tolerances are determined and documented.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: MAP 1.6
source_text: System requirements (e.g., “the system shall respect the privacy of its users”) are elicited from and understood by relevant AI actors. Design decisions take socio-technical implications into account to address AI risks.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: MAP 2
source_text: Categorization of the AI system is performed.
source_ref: NIST AI 100-1, Table 2

title: MAP 2.1
source_text: The specific task, and methods used to implement the task, that the AI system will support is defined (e.g., classifiers, generative models, recommenders).
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: MAP 2.2
source_text: Information about the AI system’s knowledge limits and how system output may be utilized and overseen by humans is documented. Documentation provides sufficient information to assist relevant AI actors when making informed decisions and taking subsequent actions.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: MAP 2.3
source_text: Scientific integrity and TEVV considerations are identified and documented, including those related to experimental design, data collection and selection (e.g., availability, representativeness, suitability), system trustworthiness, and construct validation.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: MAP 3
source_text: AI capabilities, targeted usage, goals, and expected benefits and costs compared with appropriate benchmarks are understood.
source_ref: NIST AI 100-1, Table 2

title: MAP 3.1
source_text: Potential benefits of intended AI system functionality and performance are examined and documented.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: MAP 3.2
source_text: Potential costs, including non-monetary costs, which result from expected or realized AI errors or system functionality and trustworthiness - as connected to organizational risk tolerance - are examined and documented.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: MAP 3.3
source_text: Targeted application scope is specified and documented based on the system’s capability, established context, and AI system categorization.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: MAP 3.4
source_text: Processes for operator and practitioner proficiency with AI system performance and trustworthiness – and relevant technical standards and certifications – are defined, assessed and documented.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: MAP 3.5
source_text: Processes for human oversight are defined, assessed, and documented in accordance with organizational policies from GOVERN function.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: MAP 4
source_text: Risks and benefits are mapped for all components of the AI system including third-party software and data.
source_ref: NIST AI 100-1, Table 2

title: MAP 4.1
source_text: Approaches for mapping AI technology and legal risks of its components – including the use of third-party data or software – are in place, followed, and documented, as are risks of infringement of a third-party’s intellectual property or other rights.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: MAP 4.2
source_text: Internal risk controls for components of the AI system including third-party AI technologies are identified and documented.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: MAP 5
source_text: Impacts to individuals, groups, communities, organizations, and society are characterized.
source_ref: NIST AI 100-1, Table 2

title: MAP 5.1
source_text: Likelihood and magnitude of each identified impact (both potentially beneficial and harmful) based on expected use, past uses of AI systems in similar contexts, public incident reports, feedback from those external to the team that developed or deployed the AI system, or other data are identified and documented.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: MAP 5.2
source_text: Practices and personnel for supporting regular engagement with relevant AI actors and integrating feedback about positive, negative, and unanticipated impacts are in place and documented.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: MEASURE
source_ref: NIST AI 100-1, Section 5

title: MEASURE 1
source_text: Appropriate methods and metrics are identified and applied.
source_ref: NIST AI 100-1, Table 3

title: MEASURE 1.1
source_text: Approaches and metrics for measurement of AI risks enumerated during the Map function are selected for implementation starting with the most significant AI risks. The risks or trustworthiness characteristics that will not – or cannot – be measured are properly documented.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: MEASURE 1.2
source_text: Appropriateness of AI metrics and effectiveness of existing controls is regularly assessed and updated including reports of errors and impacts on affected communities.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: MEASURE 1.3
source_text: Internal experts who did not serve as front-line developers for the system and/or independent assessors are involved in regular assessments and updates. Domain experts, users, AI actors external to the team that developed or deployed the AI system, and affected communities are consulted in support of assessments as necessary per organizational risk tolerance.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: MEASURE 2
source_text: AI systems are evaluated for trustworthy characteristics.
source_ref: NIST AI 100-1, Table 3

title: MEASURE 2.1
source_text: Test sets, metrics, and details about the tools used during TEVV are documented.
note: Playbook wording: Test sets, metrics, and details about the tools used during test, evaluation, validation, and verification (TEVV) are documented.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: MEASURE 2.2
source_text: Evaluations involving human subjects meet applicable requirements (including human subject protection) and are representative of the relevant population.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: MEASURE 2.3
source_text: AI system performance or assurance criteria are measured qualitatively or quantitatively and demonstrated for conditions similar to deployment setting(s). Measures are documented.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: MEASURE 2.4
source_text: The functionality and behavior of the AI system and its components – as identified in the MAP function – are monitored when in production.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: MEASURE 2.5
source_text: The AI system to be deployed is demonstrated to be valid and reliable. Limitations of the generalizability beyond the conditions under which the technology was developed are documented.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: MEASURE 2.6
source_text: AI system is evaluated regularly for safety risks – as identified in the MAP function. The AI system to be deployed is demonstrated to be safe, its residual negative risk does not exceed the risk tolerance, and can fail safely, particularly if made to operate beyond its knowledge limits. Safety metrics implicate system reliability and robustness, real-time monitoring, and response times for AI system failures.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: MEASURE 2.7
source_text: AI system security and resilience – as identified in the MAP function – are evaluated and documented.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: MEASURE 2.8
source_text: Risks associated with transparency and accountability – as identified in the MAP function – are examined and documented.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: MEASURE 2.9
source_text: The AI model is explained, validated, and documented, and AI system output is interpreted within its context – as identified in the MAP function – and to inform responsible use and governance.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: MEASURE 2.10
source_text: Privacy risk of the AI system – as identified in the MAP function – is examined and documented.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: MEASURE 2.11
source_text: Fairness and bias – as identified in the MAP function – are evaluated and results are documented.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: MEASURE 2.12
source_text: Environmental impact and sustainability of AI model training and management activities – as identified in the MAP function – are assessed and documented.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: MEASURE 2.13
source_text: Effectiveness of the employed TEVV metrics and processes in the MEASURE function are evaluated and documented.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: MEASURE 3
source_text: Mechanisms for tracking identified AI risks over time are in place.
source_ref: NIST AI 100-1, Table 3

title: MEASURE 3.1
source_text: Approaches, personnel, and documentation are in place to regularly identify and track existing, unanticipated, and emergent AI risks based on factors such as intended and actual performance in deployed contexts.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: MEASURE 3.2
source_text: Risk tracking approaches are considered for settings where AI risks are difficult to assess using currently available measurement techniques or where metrics are not yet available.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: MEASURE 3.3
source_text: Feedback processes for end users and impacted communities to report problems and appeal system outcomes are established and integrated into AI system evaluation metrics.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: MEASURE 4
source_text: Feedback about efficacy of measurement is gathered and assessed.
source_ref: NIST AI 100-1, Table 3

title: MEASURE 4.1
source_text: Measurement approaches for identifying AI risks are connected to deployment context(s) and informed through consultation with domain experts and other end users. Approaches are documented.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: MEASURE 4.2
source_text: Measurement results regarding AI system trustworthiness in deployment context(s) and across AI lifecycle are informed by input from domain experts and other relevant AI actors to validate whether the system is performing consistently as intended. Results are documented.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: MEASURE 4.3
source_text: Measurable performance improvements or declines based on consultations with relevant AI actors including affected communities, and field data about context-relevant risks and trustworthiness characteristics, are identified and documented.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: MANAGE
source_ref: NIST AI 100-1, Section 5

title: MANAGE 1
source_text: AI risks based on assessments and other analytical output from the MAP and MEASURE functions are prioritized, responded to, and managed.
source_ref: NIST AI 100-1, Table 4

title: MANAGE 1.1
source_text: A determination is made as to whether the AI system achieves its intended purpose and stated objectives and whether its development or deployment should proceed.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: MANAGE 1.2
source_text: Treatment of documented AI risks is prioritized based on impact, likelihood, or available resources or methods.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: MANAGE 1.3
source_text: Responses to the AI risks deemed high priority as identified by the Map function, are developed, planned, and documented. Risk response options can include mitigating, transferring, avoiding, or accepting.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: MANAGE 1.4
source_text: Negative residual risks (defined as the sum of all unmitigated risks) to both downstream acquirers of AI systems and end users are documented.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: MANAGE 2
source_text: Strategies to maximize AI benefits and minimize negative impacts are planned, prepared, implemented, documented, and informed by input from relevant AI actors.
source_ref: NIST AI 100-1, Table 4

title: MANAGE 2.1
source_text: Resources required to manage AI risks are taken into account, along with viable non-AI alternative systems, approaches, or methods – to reduce the magnitude or likelihood of potential impacts.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: MANAGE 2.2
source_text: Mechanisms are in place and applied to sustain the value of deployed AI systems.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: MANAGE 2.3
source_text: Procedures are followed to respond to and recover from a previously unknown risk when it is identified.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: MANAGE 2.4
source_text: Mechanisms are in place and applied, responsibilities are assigned and understood to supersede, disengage, or deactivate AI systems that demonstrate performance or outcomes inconsistent with intended use.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: MANAGE 3
source_text: AI risks and benefits from third-party entities are managed.
source_ref: NIST AI 100-1, Table 4

title: MANAGE 3.1
source_text: AI risks and benefits from third-party resources are regularly monitored, and risk controls are applied and documented.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: MANAGE 3.2
source_text: Pre-trained models which are used for development are monitored as part of AI system regular monitoring and maintenance.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: MANAGE 4
source_text: Risk treatments, including response and recovery, and communication plans for the identified and measured AI risks are documented and monitored regularly.
source_ref: NIST AI 100-1, Table 4

title: MANAGE 4.1
source_text: Post-deployment AI system monitoring plans are implemented, including mechanisms for capturing and evaluating input from users and other relevant AI actors, appeal and override, decommissioning, incident response, recovery, and change management.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: MANAGE 4.2
source_text: Measurable activities for continual improvements are integrated into AI system updates and include regular engagement with interested parties, including relevant AI actors.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1

title: MANAGE 4.3
source_text: Incidents and errors are communicated to relevant AI actors including affected communities. Processes for tracking, responding to, and recovering from incidents and errors are followed and documented.
source_ref: NIST AI RMF Playbook (airc.nist.gov); cross-checked with NIST AI 100-1
